observations.title: Pass 1 — specification compliance
observations.details: Independently read the complete diff from 061c97f8a01bf9e721835978b039303c5051501c to 57990ef865b51971af6469bbefc965d72c1330cb. All four methods are exposed on Expr and Series with the requested keyword-only parameters and defaults. They reuse rolling-window validation, classify expressions as ORDERABLE_WINDOW, and delegate through the existing compliant/backend abstractions. Quantile range and interpolation validation use the required ValueError prefixes. Implementations handle minimum non-null counts and centered windows, including even and oversized windows. DuckDB explicitly rejects rolling_quantile. API-reference updates and tests are within scope. No missing functionality, unrelated scope expansion, or misinterpretation was identified in the inspected code and exercised backends.

observations.title: Pass 2 — code quality
observations.details: After the specification pass, checked backend delegation, existing rolling conventions, naming, boundary validation, type annotations, null handling, test coverage, and documentation. The implementation follows the existing architecture and does not introduce dependencies. Tests exercise real backends rather than mocks, including grouped ordering, nulls, interpolation, invalid arguments, empty inputs, and Arrow chunk boundaries. No blocking quality defects were found.

observations.title: Suggestion — benchmark Arrow rolling aggregation on large windows
observations.details: The shared Arrow fallback slices and recounts/reaggregates each window, giving approximately O(number_of_rows * window_size) work for min/max and at least repeated window traversal for median/quantile. This is functionally correct in the exercised cases and is not a specification blocker. As optional follow-up, benchmark realistic large inputs and consider a specialized moving-extrema algorithm or document the fallback's performance characteristics.

findings.title: Register all four methods in the pandas grouped-window dispatch
findings.requirement: The new Expr rolling methods must follow the backend patterns of rolling_sum, rolling_mean, rolling_std, and rolling_var. The existing public Expr.over(partition_by, order_by=...) interface supports grouped rolling windows on pandas.
findings.location: narwhals/expr.py:1928-1935 (and the other new rolling nodes); narwhals/_pandas_like/expr.py:38-41,282-291; tests/expr_and_series/rolling_statistics_test.py:194-195
findings.evidence: With df = nw.from_native(pd.DataFrame({'a': [1., 3., 10., 20.], 'g': ['x', 'x', 'y', 'y'], 'i': [0, 1, 2, 3]})), df.select(nw.col('a').rolling_sum(2, min_samples=1).over('g', order_by='i')) returns [1., 4., 10., 30.] and rolling_mean returns [1., 2., 10., 15.]. Replacing rolling_sum with rolling_min, rolling_max, rolling_median, or rolling_quantile (quantile=0.5) raises NotImplementedError: Unsupported function: rolling_<method> in `over` context. The new names are absent from WINDOW_FUNCTIONS_TO_PANDAS_EQUIVALENT, so PandasLikeExpr.over rejects them. The newly added grouped test incorrectly skips pandas with the claim that grouped rolling is unsupported. This is contradicted by the existing implementation and rolling_sum grouped tests, rather than an established backend limitation.
findings.repair: Add the four names to the pandas window dispatch and forward quantile/interpolation to the grouped rolling quantile call (the existing generic branch calls rolling methods without arguments). Remove the incorrect pandas skip and cover grouped windows, including non-default quantile and interpolation. Expected results for the reproduction are min [1., 1., 10., 10.], max [1., 3., 10., 20.], and median/quantile(0.5) [1., 2., 10., 15.].

findings.title: Avoid reconstructing Arrow discrete quantiles as float64 Python values
findings.requirement: rolling_quantile must compute valid numeric rolling quantiles with each of the five supported interpolation modes, following the existing quantile/backend conventions. Valid Int64 inputs must not fail solely because the result is an integer not exactly representable as float64.
findings.evidence: Reproduced with s = nw.from_native(pa.chunked_array([[2**53 + 1, 2**53 + 3]]), series_only=True). For each interpolation in ('lower', 'higher', 'nearest'), s.rolling_quantile(2, quantile=0.5, interpolation=interpolation) raises pyarrow.ArrowInvalid: Integer value ... is outside of the range exactly representable by a IEEE 754 double precision value. The existing s.quantile(0.5, interpolation=...) succeeds, returning respectively 9007199254740993, 9007199254740995, and 9007199254740993. pc.quantile returns an integer scalar for these interpolation modes; _rolling_aggregate converts it to a Python int and then passes it to pa.chunked_array(..., type=pa.float64()), whose conversion rejects these values. The same path also fails for Decimal inputs, e.g. pa.chunked_array([[Decimal('1.00'), Decimal('2.00')]], type=pa.decimal128(10, 2)), with ArrowInvalid: Could not convert Decimal('1.00') ... tried to convert to double. Linear and midpoint interpolation succeed on both examples, so this is specifically the forced reconstruction of discrete quantile results.
findings.repair: Preserve the native quantile result type for discrete interpolation, or perform a deliberate Arrow-native conversion to the documented output type rather than implicit Python-value reconstruction. Add Series and Expr regression tests for large signed/unsigned integers and Decimal values across interpolation modes. Do not catch the exception and replace valid results with null.

observations: The implementation adds all four requested public methods to Expr and Series, API-reference entries, shared argument validation, ORDERABLE_WINDOW expression classification, and backend delegation. No unrelated feature work was identified in the requested commit diff.
Pass 1 (spec compliance) fails on the two behavioral defects above. Pass 2 (code quality) was not performed, as required by the sequential review policy.

The added rolling_statistics_test.py suite passed on pandas, pandas nullable, pandas Arrow-backed, eager/lazy Polars, PyArrow, and DuckDB: 1052 passed, 208 skipped, 48 xfailed. Command: python -m pytest tests/expr_and_series/rolling_statistics_test.py --constructors='pandas,pandas[nullable],pandas[pyarrow],polars[eager],polars[lazy],pyarrow,duckdb' -q -o addopts=''. Output saved in /tmp/rolling-tests.log.
The new suite also ran with --constructors='sqlframe': 113 passed, 143 skipped. Output saved in /tmp/rolling-sqlframe.log.

Existing rolling_sum, rolling_mean, rolling_var, and rolling_std suites passed for the seven available constructors: 533 passed, 25 skipped, 28 xfailed. Output saved in /tmp/rolling-regression.log. These tests independently establish existing grouped pandas rolling support and the established centered-even-window alignment.

The new suite exercises default and explicit min_samples, null exclusion, centered/trailing windows, argument errors and required error-message prefixes, ordered lazy windows, DuckDB quantile rejection, empty/all-null numeric inputs, and Arrow chunk boundaries. Those covered cases passed; the grouped pandas skips and small numeric fixtures leave the reported defects undetected.

Repository documentation independently confirms that lazy order-dependent expressions require over(order_by=...). The new Expr methods use the same ORDERABLE_WINDOW classification as existing rolling methods. The explicit DuckDB rolling_quantile rejection matches the original request. Existing quantile documentation permits backend interpolation differences, so nearest tie-breaking differences were not treated as a defect.
